question: Which statement correctly describes a feature of the Vijayanagara Empire?

options.text: Hazara Rama temple was meant for public worship
Mahanavami Dibba had a wooden superstructure
Sacred centre lay south of Tungabhadra

solution:
The correct answer is __**Lotus Mahal reflects Indo-Islamic influence**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Lotus Mahal**, located in the royal enclosure of Hampi (the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire), is an architectural marvel reflecting a blend of **Indo-Islamic architectural styles**.
 
• It features **Islamic-style arches and domes** integrated with the traditional Indian temple-style elements like multi-layered pyramidal towers.
 
• The Mahal is named "Lotus Mahal" because its structure resembles a blooming lotus flower, particularly in the design of its arches and domes.
 
• This structure is believed to have been used as a **council chamber or a place of recreation** for the royal women of Vijayanagara.
 
• The Lotus Mahal is built with a combination of **lime mortar and brick**, a reflection of the advanced construction techniques of the Vijayanagara Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hazara Rama Temple**:

 
 
• The Hazara Rama Temple, located in Hampi, was **not meant for public worship**. It was a private temple of the royal family of Vijayanagara.
 
• The temple is renowned for its intricate bas-reliefs depicting scenes from the **Ramayana** and processions of horses, elephants, and soldiers.
 
• Its name, "Hazara Rama," translates to "A Thousand Ramas," referencing the numerous Ramayana panels decorating the temple walls.
 
 
 
• **Mahanavami Dibba**:
 
 
• The Mahanavami Dibba, or "Great Platform," is a massive stone platform in Hampi used by the kings of Vijayanagara for royal ceremonies and public appearances.
 
• It did have a **wooden superstructure** that has not survived over time, but the stone base remains intact.
 
• The platform is adorned with intricate carvings of processions, festivities, and various cultural activities of the Vijayanagara period.
 
 
 
• **Sacred Centre of Vijayanagara**:
 
 
• The sacred centre of Hampi is located on the northern bank of the **Tungabhadra River**, not south of it, as mentioned in the option.
 
• This area is home to important temples like the **Virupaksha Temple** (dedicated to Lord Shiva) and the **Vittala Temple**, showcasing the architectural excellence of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• The sacred centre was the religious heart of the empire, attracting pilgrims and devotees from far and wide.
